cases.request: Assess whether the proposed account-deletion protection satisfies the stated invariant, using only these local test records.
records: Invariant: possession of an old session alone must not supply proof for account deletion.
The local handler accepts a fresh password sign-in within its configured recent-auth window.
A disposable passwordless account has an old session. The attacker has that session but no mailbox or provider access.
Using the old session, the attacker adds a first password. Auth returns 200.
Signing in with that new password returns a fresh password authentication timestamp.
The deletion endpoint then returns 200. Controller readback finds the synthetic account absent and the unrelated control account present.
The control server requires the current password for accounts that already have one.

cases.request: Assess the account-binding behavior and state exactly what these two executions establish.
records: Two disposable accounts, A and B, both have valid recent email-code sign-ins.
The user opens A's deletion confirmation. The client checks A and captures A's access token.
Before dispatch, the shared SDK's current session changes to B.
Execution X supplies A's captured token explicitly. The real local endpoint deletes A; controller readback confirms B survives.
Execution Y omits the explicit header and lets the SDK supply its current session. The endpoint deletes B; controller readback confirms A survives.
The endpoint always derives its target from the validated bearer token and ignores a body user_id.
